biblical-theology-study.name: Biblical Theology Study
biblical-theology-study.description: A theme traced through the unfolding story of Scripture.

theme.title: Theme
theme.guidance: The theme being traced and why it matters.

old-testament.title: Old Testament
old-testament.guidance: Where the theme begins and how it develops in the Law, Prophets and Writings.

gospels.title: Gospels
gospels.guidance: How the theme comes to Christ in the Gospels.

epistles.title: Epistles
epistles.guidance: How the apostles take up and apply the theme.

canonical-development.title: Canonical Development
canonical-development.guidance: How the theme grows and changes across the canon.

fulfilment.title: Fulfilment / Consummation
fulfilment.guidance: Where and how the theme reaches its fulfilment or completion.

synthesis.title: Synthesis
synthesis.guidance: The whole-Bible picture in a few sentences.

teaching.title: Teaching
teaching.guidance: How to teach this theme faithfully and clearly.

new-testament.title: New Testament
new-testament.guidance: How the theme comes to Christ and how the apostles take it up.

passage-study.name: Passage Study
passage-study.description: A careful study of one passage, from the text itself to what it means for faith and life.

text.title: Text
text.guidance: The passage being studied, and any translation notes.

context.title: Context
context.guidance: Where the passage sits: the book, the surrounding argument, the historical setting.

observations.title: Observations
observations.guidance: What does the text say? Repeated words, connectors, contrasts, commands, questions.

structure.title: Structure
structure.guidance: How the passage is built: its movements, main clauses and turning points.

exegesis.title: Exegesis
exegesis.guidance: What did the text mean for its first readers? Key words, grammar, difficult phrases.

theology.title: Theology
theology.guidance: What the passage teaches about God, Christ, salvation and the life of faith.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: How the truth of the passage bears on belief, worship and life today.

audience.title: Audience
audience.guidance: Who will hear this teaching, what they need, and what may hinder them.

teaching.title: Teaching
teaching.guidance: Main idea, outline, illustrations and how to communicate it with love.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.guidance: What did the text mean for its first readers? Key words, grammar, difficult phrases.

key-words.title: Key Words
key-words.guidance: Words that carry the passage: what they mean here and elsewhere.

related-scripture.title: Related Scripture
related-scripture.guidance: Other passages that explain, echo or fulfil this one.

open-questions.title: Open Questions
open-questions.guidance: What you do not yet understand, to come back to.

systematic-theology-study.name: Systematic Theology Study
systematic-theology-study.description: A doctrine studied from Scripture, the church's witness and competing positions.

doctrine.title: Doctrine
doctrine.guidance: The doctrine under study, stated plainly.

key-texts.title: Key Biblical Texts
key-texts.guidance: The passages on which the doctrine rests.

historical-theology.title: Historical Theology
historical-theology.guidance: How the church has understood the doctrine through its history.

confessional-witness.title: Confessional Witness
confessional-witness.guidance: What the creeds and confessions say.

alternative-positions.title: Alternative Positions
alternative-positions.guidance: Other views, fairly stated, with their reasons.

conclusions.title: Conclusions
conclusions.guidance: Your conclusions and how firmly you hold them.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: Why this doctrine matters for faith and life.

teaching-study.name: Teaching / Sermon Preparation
teaching-study.description: From the text to a sermon or lesson prepared for real people.

main-idea.title: Main Idea
main-idea.guidance: The one main thing the text says, in one sentence.

exegesis.title: Exegesis
exegesis.guidance: What the text meant for its first readers.

theology.title: Theology
theology.guidance: What the text teaches about God and his ways.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.guidance: What the text aims to do in its hearers.

audience.title: Audience
audience.guidance: Who will hear this, and what they need.

structure.title: Structure
structure.guidance: How the teaching will move from beginning to end.

illustrations.title: Illustrations
illustrations.guidance: Pictures and examples that serve the text.

teaching-outline.title: Teaching Outline
teaching-outline.guidance: The outline you will teach from.

topical-study.name: Topical Bible Study
topical-study.description: Answer a focused biblical question by interpreting relevant passages in context before drawing conclusions.

topic.title: Topic and questions
topic.guidance: State the topic, its boundaries and the questions the study should answer. Avoid starting with a conclusion.

key-passages.title: Relevant Scripture
key-passages.guidance: Gather representative passages, including those that qualify or appear to challenge an initial view. Note why each is relevant.

biblical-context.title: Biblical Context
biblical-context.guidance: Where and how the topic arises across the Bible.

main-themes.title: Compare and group findings
main-themes.guidance: Group the passages by their actual teaching, noting agreements, differences, development and remaining questions.

difficult-passages.title: Difficult or balancing texts
difficult-passages.guidance: Examine apparently conflicting passages without ignoring their context or forcing a superficial harmonisation.

theology.title: Theology
theology.guidance: How the passages fit together into coherent teaching.

conclusions.title: Biblical conclusions
conclusions.guidance: Answer the opening questions with references. Distinguish what Scripture clearly teaches from reasonable inference and unresolved issues.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: Identify concrete implications for belief, worship, relationships and action, grounded in the conclusions.

passage-study.title: Examine the passages
passage-study.guidance: Read each text in its literary, historical and covenantal context. Distinguish direct teaching, narrative description, inference and application.

biblical-theology.title: Place in the whole Bible
biblical-theology.guidance: Where relevant, consider how the teaching unfolds through the covenants and relates to Christ and the gospel without imposing a connection.

word-study.name: Biblical Word Study
word-study.description: Investigate a biblical word in its original language and contexts without assuming one meaning in every occurrence.

word.title: Word and question
word.guidance: Identify the Hebrew or Greek lemma, spelling and the particular passage or question. A translated English word may represent several different original words.

occurrences.title: Occurrences and translations
occurrences.guidance: Find representative occurrences of this lemma and note how translators render it. Distinguish the lemma from inflected forms and other words with similar translations.

immediate-contexts.title: Immediate Contexts
immediate-contexts.guidance: How each important use is shaped by its sentence and paragraph.

semantic-range.title: Range of meanings
semantic-range.guidance: Describe possible meanings from contextual evidence. Do not derive meaning solely from etymology or import every possible sense into one occurrence.

key-passages.title: Passages in context
key-passages.guidance: Read each significant occurrence in its sentence, paragraph, genre and historical setting. Record which sense best fits and why.

theological-significance.title: Biblical-theological connections
theological-significance.guidance: Compare related biblical teaching while keeping each passage's own meaning distinct.

conclusions.title: Meaning and conclusion
conclusions.guidance: Explain what the word means in the passage under study, citing textual evidence. State uncertainties and avoid making the word carry more theology than the passage supports.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: What follows for belief and life from the passage's teaching, rather than from a dictionary definition alone?

grammar.title: Grammar and syntax
grammar.guidance: Where helpful, examine grammatical form, syntax and discourse function. Use reputable linguistic tools; original-language expertise is optional.

pozetek-study.name: Guided Passage Study
pozetek-study.description: A guided study of any passage: observation (Persons, Place, Time, Events, Text context), interpretation (Explanations), the central message (Core), and then a separate personal application.

persons.title: Persons
persons.guidance: Who appears in the text, who speaks, who acts, and to whom is the message addressed?
persons.goal: Get to know everyone involved before interpreting anything. Record only what the text itself says.
persons.example: Hosea proclaims God’s word to Israel/Ephraim; the focus is God’s relationship with his people. Egypt and Assyria belong to the historical background that is addressed.

author.label: Author
author.help: Who wrote or spoke this text, as far as the text or its book says?

speaker.label: Speaker(s)
speaker.help: Who is speaking in this passage? Does the speaker change?

addressees.label: Addressees
addressees.help: To whom is the message directed?

people.label: People and groups
people.help: Add each person or group named or implied. Note the verse and what each one does or is.

relationships.label: Relationships
relationships.help: How are those involved related to one another? Who stands over, with or against whom?

open-questions.label: Open questions
open-questions.help: What about the people in this text is still unclear?

place.title: Place
place.guidance: Which places and spatial or cultural relationships matter for the text?
place.goal: Notice where things happen or are spoken of. Keep what the text says apart from what you learn from outside sources.
place.example: The northern kingdom of Israel is the context; Egypt recalls Israel’s deliverance, Assyria stands for political threat.

places.label: Places named in the text
places.help: List each place the text names. Note the verse and what role it plays.

background.label: Geographic and cultural background
background.help: What does outside research add? Say where each piece of information comes from, so it stays distinct from the text.

unclear.label: Unclear places
unclear.help: Which place references are still uncertain?

time.title: Time
time.guidance: When does the text take place, and which historical circumstances matter?
time.goal: Place the text in time. Mark what the text states and what is a historical placement that may be uncertain.
time.example: Hosea’s ministry in the 8th century BC and the growing Assyrian influence are relevant background information.

stated.label: Time stated in the text
stated.help: Which dates, seasons, sequences or phrases such as “then” and “in those days” does the text give?

historical.label: Historical setting
historical.help: What do you know about the period? Mark uncertain points as uncertain.

source.label: Source for the historical setting
source.help: Where does this information come from?

sequence.label: Course of time
sequence.help: How does time move within the passage? What comes before, during and after?

prophecy.label: Prophecy: past, present, future
prophecy.help: If the text is prophetic: what looks back, what describes the present situation, what announces the future?

events.title: Events
events.guidance: What happens? How do events or statements unfold?
events.goal: Follow the movement of the text section by section. The outline is yours to propose and to change.
events.example: A possible outline of Hosea 11: vv. 1–4 care; vv. 5–7 unfaithfulness and judgment; vv. 8–9 compassion; vv. 10–11 return and restoration.

passages.label: Sections of the text
passages.help: Divide the text into sections. For each, give the verses, what happens or is said, and what it means for the course of the whole.

parts.meaning: Meaning in the course of the text

turning-points.label: Turning points
turning-points.help: Where does the direction of the text change?

contrasts.label: Contrasts
contrasts.help: Which opposites or tensions does the text set against each other?

context.title: Text context
context.guidance: How does the passage fit into the chapter, the whole book and the rest of Scripture?
context.goal: See the passage in its surroundings, from the nearest verses outward, and notice where it ends.
context.example: Israel’s unfaithfulness and the covenant relationship shape Hosea; chapter 11 adds the image of the caring father and his child.

immediate.label: Immediate context
immediate.help: What comes directly before and after the passage, and how does it connect?

book.label: Context in the book
book.help: What is the book about, and where does the passage stand in its argument or story?

canon.label: Context in the whole Bible
canon.help: How does the passage relate to the rest of Scripture and its storyline?

parallels.label: Parallel passages
parallels.help: Add related passages. Say what each contributes to understanding this text.

limits.label: Limits of the passage
limits.help: Where does the unit begin and end, and why there?

explanations.title: Explanations
explanations.guidance: Which terms, statements or interpretive problems need clarifying?
explanations.goal: Collect questions from the text, check them against evidence, and record the answers you can support. Leave open what is still open.
explanations.example: What role do Egypt and Assyria play? How do judgment and compassion belong together? What does “God and not man” (Hos 11:9) mean?

questions.label: Question log
questions.help: Add each question. Record the verse, the evidence you checked, your answer, and whether the question is still open.

terms.label: Important terms
terms.help: Which words need explaining? What do they mean here, in this context?

explanations.label: Possible explanations
explanations.help: Where more than one explanation is possible, state each with its reasons.

sources.label: Sources
sources.help: Which sources did you use? Note them so you can find them again.

core.title: Core
core.guidance: What is the central message of exactly this passage?
core.goal: Name the core in three steps: what the text is about, what it says about that, and one concise sentence. You may fill them in any order.
core.example: Subject: God’s relationship to his unfaithful people. Statement: God’s care, just judgment and compassion. Theme: God’s love for Israel shows itself in his care, in just judgment, and in a compassion that opens a future.

subject.label: Text subject — What is it about?
subject.help: Name the subject in a few words, without yet saying what the text claims about it.

statement.label: Text statement — What does the text say about it?
statement.help: Summarise what the passage says about its subject, as it says it.

theme.label: Text theme — One concise sentence
theme.help: Join subject and statement in one sentence that you could test against every verse.

application.title: Personal application
application.guidance: What does the truth you found mean for you? Keep it apart from the observation and interpretation above.
application.goal: Respond to the text in a way that stays tied to what it says. This is a closing step of its own, not another letter of POZETEK.
application.example: God’s love for his people rests in his nature, not in Israel’s faithfulness. Even though Israel turns away, God shows compassion in the midst of judgment. That challenges us to recognise our own substitute securities and to trust God anew. Love received should also shape how we treat people who do not return love and care (cf. 1 John 4:8, 19).

truth.label: Truth recognised
truth.help: Which truth of the text stays valid for every reader?

examination.label: Personal examination
examination.help: Where does this truth challenge, comfort or correct your own thinking and life?

response.label: Concrete response
response.help: What will you do: believe, repent, trust, obey, pray, love? Make it specific.

limits.label: Limits of the transfer
limits.help: What differs between the original situation and today? What must not be carried over directly?

ten-step-exegesis.name: Ten-Step Bible Study
ten-step-exegesis.description: A thorough passage study following the ten interpretive steps presented by Helge Stadelmann and Thomas Richter. Guidance and the optional Matthew 8:18–27 example are independently written.

step-01-familiarity.title: 1 — Become familiar with the text
step-01-familiarity.guidance: Read the whole passage several times, including in more than one translation. Identify its initial movement and record questions without answering them prematurely.
step-01-familiarity.goal: First impressions and unresolved questions, not a finished interpretation.
step-01-familiarity.example: Matthew 8:18–27 contains two encounters about following Jesus, followed by the calming of the storm. Initial questions include the cost of discipleship, the command to let the dead bury their dead, the disciples’ little faith, and the identity of the one who commands wind and sea.

first-impression.label: First impression
first-impression.help: What seems to be the passage's main concern on an initial reading?

movement.label: How the text develops
movement.help: What scenes, changes or lines of thought are visible?

questions.label: Questions to investigate
questions.help: Record questions now; do not force an early answer.

step-02-text.title: 2 — Establish the textual basis
step-02-text.guidance: Compare translations and relevant textual notes. Distinguish decisions about rendering the text from differences among manuscripts; document uncertainty rather than inventing certainty.
step-02-text.goal: A documented basis for reading this text, with important translation questions marked.
step-02-text.example: In Matthew 8:24, translations describe a violent storm or disturbance on the lake. The Greek wording emphasises its intensity. Its precise force must be weighed in context, not expanded into events the passage does not report.

comparisons.label: Translation comparisons
comparisons.help: Note actual wording differences and whether they matter.

manuscripts.label: Relevant manuscript notes
manuscripts.help: Record only variants supported by a trustworthy textual source.

basis.label: Working text
basis.help: Which text or translation will you primarily examine, and why?

uncertainties.label: Unsettled questions
uncertainties.help: What cannot yet be decided from the available evidence?

step-03-situation.title: 3 — Clarify the original communication situation
step-03-situation.guidance: Ask who wrote to whom, when, where, and why. Research historical and cultural details that actually help explain this passage; distinguish evidence from inference.
step-03-situation.goal: The relevant historical setting, not a collection of unrelated background facts.
step-03-situation.example: Matthew presents Jesus as the promised Messiah. The events occur during his ministry in Galilee. Following a teacher then meant more than attending lessons; Jesus calls people to follow him personally and without treating comfort as the highest good.

author-audience.label: Author and intended audience
author-audience.help: What can reasonably be established about writer and readers?

time-place.label: Time and location
time-place.help: Distinguish the setting of the reported event from the time of writing.

purpose.label: Purpose of communication
purpose.help: Why was the book or passage written or spoken?

background.label: Relevant historical and cultural background
background.help: What facts clarify this passage, and which are only hypotheses?

sources.label: Sources and degree of confidence
sources.help: Cite the Bible passage, introduction or reference work you consulted.

step-04-context.title: 4 — Understand the context
step-04-context.guidance: Trace the passage's boundaries and its place in the surrounding verses, the book, parallel accounts, and the Bible as a whole. Let the nearest context guide distant comparisons.
step-04-context.goal: Explain how the passage contributes to its book and how its limits were chosen.
step-04-context.example: After the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7), Matthew 8 portrays Jesus' authority through healings. Two calls to discipleship precede the boat scene: in 8:23 the disciples follow Jesus into the boat. The episodes can also be studied separately.

boundaries.label: Passage boundaries
boundaries.help: Where does this unit begin and end? What indicates the boundaries?

nearby.label: Immediate context
nearby.help: What comes directly before and after?

book.label: Place in the book
book.help: How does this unit contribute to the book's flow?

parallels.label: Related passages
parallels.help: List parallels without assuming they are identical.

whole-bible.label: Wider biblical context
whole-bible.help: How does the unit relate to Scripture's wider testimony?

step-05-genre.title: 5 — Examine the type of text
step-05-genre.guidance: Identify the literary genre, form, and significant techniques such as contrast, repetition, dialogue, or parallelism. Explain how they convey the message, without imposing a pattern.
step-05-genre.goal: An interpretation shaped by the way this passage communicates.
step-05-genre.example: Matthew 8:18–22 contains two short dialogues centred on Jesus' replies; verses 23–27 form a miracle narrative. The disciples fear while Jesus sleeps; the fierce storm gives way to calm; helpless people face Jesus' authority.

genre.label: Literary genre
genre.help: Is it narrative, poetry, prophecy, letter, law, parable or another genre?

form.label: Form within the genre
form.help: What kind of narrative, speech or argument is it?

features.label: Literary features
features.help: What can actually be observed in the wording?

interpretation.label: Implications for interpretation
interpretation.help: How should this literary form shape your reading?

step-06-language.title: 6 — Examine words and sentences
step-06-language.guidance: Study important terms, sentence connections, contrasts, and actions in context. Use original-language tools carefully; a dictionary entry by itself does not establish meaning.
step-06-language.goal: Explain significant wording and relationships within the passage.
step-06-language.example: In Matthew 8:20, animals have resting places but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head: the contrast challenges expectations of secure comfort. In 8:21–22, the issue is the priority of Jesus' call. The father's circumstances cannot be established with certainty from these verses.

terms.label: Important terms
terms.help: Determine meaning from use in this sentence and context.

connections.label: Sentence relationships
connections.help: Look for contrasts, reasons, conditions, actions and their objects.

sources.label: Language tools consulted
sources.help: Record translations, lexicons or grammatical sources.

step-07-flow.title: 7 — Trace the train of thought
step-07-flow.guidance: Return to the complete passage. Observe who speaks and acts, how clauses or scenes connect, and where the argument changes. Draft a text diagram and a justified outline.
step-07-flow.goal: A clear outline drawn from the text, not imposed on it.
step-07-flow.example: One possible outline of Matthew 8:18–27: vv. 18–20, the cost of following Jesus; vv. 21–22, the priority of his call; vv. 23–25, disciples follow him into danger; vv. 26–27, Jesus reveals his authority over wind and sea.

flow.label: Sequence and connections
flow.help: How does each part lead into the next?

outline.label: Outline of the passage
outline.help: Give each segment a short, text-supported heading.

diagram.label: Text diagram or structural notes
diagram.help: Optional: sketch the logic or refer to a diagram in the study workspace.

step-08-theology.title: 8 — Clarify theological questions
step-08-theology.guidance: Investigate theological questions first in the passage, then in its immediate and wider biblical context. Scripture interprets Scripture; keep unresolved questions visible.
step-08-theology.goal: Interpret theological claims in a way that is faithful to this text and the whole Bible.
step-08-theology.example: Matthew 8:22 raises the question of honouring parents: Jesus affirms that duty elsewhere (Matthew 15:4–6), so his words cannot abolish it universally. The storm narrative invites comparison with God's rule over the sea (Psalm 89:10; 107:23–30), sharpening the question of Jesus' identity.

questions.label: Theological questions
questions.help: Give evidence, a reasoned answer and a clear status.

cross-references.label: Cross-references
cross-references.help: Explain their contribution, not merely their similarity.

coherence.label: Theological coherence
coherence.help: How does the reading fit the Bible's testimony without silencing this passage?

unresolved.label: Questions still open
unresolved.help: Which questions require more study or remain uncertain?

step-09-message.title: 9 — Formulate the central message
step-09-message.guidance: Distinguish the subject (what the text is about), the statement (what it says about that), and the theme (a clear sentence expressing both). Test the theme against the whole passage.
step-09-message.goal: A brief and defensible statement of the passage's central message.
step-09-message.example: Subject: following Jesus in view of his demands and authority. Statement: Jesus calls for priority over security and other obligations; his followers may trust his authority even in danger. Theme: Following Jesus requires wholehearted commitment and trust in the Lord whose authority is greater than the dangers his disciples face.

subject.label: Text subject — What is it about?
subject.help: Name the topic without yet making the text's claim.

statement.label: Text statement — What does it say?
statement.help: Summarise the passage's claim about this subject.

theme.label: Text theme — One sentence
theme.help: Combine subject and statement in a concise proposition.

text-check.label: Check against the whole passage
text-check.help: Does every part support this theme? What may need refinement?

step-10-application.title: 10 — Understand and apply the meaning today
step-10-application.guidance: Move from original meaning to responsible present-day application. Consider what differs after Christ's death, resurrection, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit. Form a concrete response without equating every historical detail with today.
step-10-application.goal: A faithful, concrete response grounded in the text and attentive to its original setting.
step-10-application.example: Matthew 8 calls readers to examine where comfort or security outranks trust in Christ. The disciples' circumstances during Jesus' earthly ministry cannot simply be reproduced today, but his claim on discipleship remains. Confidence rests in Christ's authority, not in the absence of difficulty.

enduring-truth.label: Enduring truth
enduring-truth.help: Which truth applies beyond the original situation?

differences.label: Differences between then and now
differences.help: Consider covenant and redemptive-historical differences as well as culture.

examination.label: Personal examination
examination.help: Where does this text challenge, correct, encourage or comfort?

response.label: Concrete response
response.help: What is an honest, specific next response of faith or obedience?

limits.label: Limits of application
limits.help: What must not be transferred directly or promised without warrant?

biblical-character-study.name: Biblical Character Study
biblical-character-study.description: Study a biblical person's life and character through the relevant passages.

person.title: Person and passages
person.guidance: Identify the person, name variants, and principal biblical references. Distinguish this person from others with the same name.

setting.title: Historical and biblical setting
setting.guidance: Locate the person in the biblical story, including their family, relationships, responsibilities and circumstances. Mark disputed dates or identifications as uncertain.

life.title: Life, words and actions
life.guidance: Trace key events chronologically where possible. Record what the text actually says, with references; do not assume the narrative gives a complete biography.

character.title: Character and decisions
character.guidance: Examine actions, words, strengths, weaknesses and recurring patterns. Distinguish the narrator's explicit evaluation from your own inference about motives.

god.title: God's work and the biblical evaluation
god.guidance: How does God act in this person's life, and how does Scripture evaluate their choices? Consider the person's place in the wider biblical story without treating every detail as exemplary.

conclusion.title: Main findings
conclusion.guidance: Summarise the person's significance with supporting passages, including uncertainties and tensions.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: What does Scripture teach through this life about faith, obedience, sin, grace and relationships? Apply the text rather than imitating every recorded action.

comparisons.title: Related figures and passages
comparisons.guidance: Compare relevant people or passages only where the connections illuminate the text.

whole-book-study.name: Whole-Book Bible Study
whole-book-study.description: Read an entire biblical book, trace its structure and message, and apply its teaching.

reading.title: Read the whole book
reading.guidance: Read the book through, preferably more than once and in more than one translation. Note first impressions, recurring words, tone, genre and questions before consulting commentaries.

setting.title: Author, audience and setting
setting.guidance: Investigate authorship, recipients, historical and geographical context, occasion and purpose. Separate statements in the book from scholarly proposals and unresolved questions.

overview.title: Overview and central concerns
overview.guidance: Record main people, events, themes, key verses and the book's broad movement. Avoid treating every recurring word as the main theme.

outline.title: Structure and content
outline.guidance: Divide the book into natural literary units with passage references and brief headings. Explain how each section contributes to the whole.

argument.title: Message and development
argument.guidance: Trace the narrative or argument across sections, attending to genre, contrasts, promises, commands and how the conclusion relates to the opening.

synthesis.title: Central message
synthesis.guidance: State the book's subject, what it teaches about that subject, and its overall message, supported by the text.

application.title: Application
application.guidance: Consider implications for belief, worship and life that follow from the book's message and its place in the whole Bible.

further.title: Further study
further.guidance: List difficult passages, historical questions, relevant cross-references and sources to revisit.

templates.intro: A Bible Teaching template is what a new teaching starts with: its format, and the points, questions or steps it begins with. A teaching takes a copy when it is made, so changing or deleting a template never changes a teaching.
templates.confirm: Delete the template “{{name}}”? Bible Teachings already made from it are not affected.
templates.pointsHint: Leave a title empty to name it in each teaching.
templates.none: Nothing yet: a teaching made with this template starts empty.

saveTemplate.group: Save this teaching’s structure as a template
saveTemplate.name: Name of the template

keeps.points: The template keeps the format and as many main points as this teaching has, in order. The points start without titles.
keeps.generalPoints: The template keeps the format and as many main points as this teaching has, in order. The points start without titles.
keeps.questions: The template keeps the format and as many questions as this teaching has. The questions start empty.
keeps.steps: The template keeps the format and the steps in order, each with its title and kind.
keeps.blocks: The template keeps the format and the sections and blocks this teaching starts with, in order. Nothing written in the blocks comes with it.

saveTemplate.notKept: Nothing you wrote comes with it: not the audience, purpose, message, introduction, conclusion or notes; nothing written under a point, question or step; no passages, kept material or notes from your study.
saveTemplate.saved: Saved as your template “{{name}}”. You can choose it for your next Bible Teaching, and change it in Settings → Templates.
saveTemplate.tooMany: A template can start with at most {{max}} points, questions or steps, and this teaching has more. Make the template in Settings → Templates instead.
saveTemplate.tooManyBlocks: A template can start with at most {{max}} blocks, and this teaching has more. Make the template in Settings → Templates instead.

teaching.formatLegend: What would you like to prepare?

message.name: Message
message.hint: A sermon, talk or devotion: a central message, an introduction, main points and a conclusion.

group.name: Group Bible study
group.hint: Led by discussion: an opening, the Bible text, questions and answers, and a closing.

lesson.name: Interactive lesson
lesson.hint: For children, youth or adults: steps such as Bible reading, explanation, questions, an activity or a picture.

teaching.notesPrivate: Only for you: never part of the Materials for your listeners or group.

blocks.leaderOnly: For you as the leader. It is left out of handouts and slides unless you mark it for participants.
blocks.empty: This teaching is empty. Add a section or a writing area when you are ready.
blocks.templateHint: Add, reorder, duplicate and rename the sections and blocks a new teaching starts with. What you write in a teaching is not kept in the template.

eva.name: Bible Study — EVA
eva.hint: For a group: observe the passage, understand it, then ask what follows.

erkennen.title: Observation
erkennen.guidance: What does the passage actually say, and what can the group discover for themselves? Optional Campus Connect 3×3 prompts: read it together, listen as it is read again, retell it in your own words.

verstehen.title: Comprehension
verstehen.guidance: Meaning in the literary, historical and biblical context, and the central message. Optional Campus Connect 3×3 prompts: what became important, what this says about God and about people, how the context helps.

anwenden.title: Application
anwenden.guidance: What follows for faith, understanding, decisions, behaviour and relationships. Optional Campus Connect 3×3 prompts: what changes in how we think and live, what we will do, whom this could encourage.

sermonTalk.name: Sermon / Talk
sermonTalk.hint: Introduction, the main part, and a conclusion. Write it straight through, or add outline points.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.guidance: How you will begin. A central message, the people you are speaking to, and the purpose can be added as blocks if you want them.

main.title: Main part
main.guidance: The body of the sermon or talk. Add outline points if you want a structure beside the continuous writing.

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.guidance: How you will close, and what response is fitting.

bibleLesson.name: Bible Lesson — Children / Youth
bibleLesson.hint: One lesson for children or young people. Age changes how you tell it, not what the passage means.

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.guidance: Optional: note the age you are preparing for, how long you have, and what you hope they take away. Age changes how you tell the story, not what the passage means. Add time or learning-objective blocks only if you want them.

story.title: Story
story.guidance: Tell the passage in a way that fits the age. The meaning stays the one the text has.

explain.title: Explanation
explain.guidance: Say what the passage means, in words they can follow. Do not replace the text’s meaning with a simpler idea.

questions.title: Questions
questions.guidance: Questions the group hears, and your own notes about answers to listen for. Those notes stay with you.

activity.title: Activity
activity.guidance: Something they do with what they have heard.

reflect.title: Reflection
reflect.guidance: What they can take into faith, choices and relationships.
